# Build, release, and the docs site

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
  [-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns core CSS
  correctness; cssdoc owns documentation comments. `lint:css` and `lint:cssdoc` run in `ready`, and
  both are wired into the `vite.config.ts` staged hook.

## Local component accessibility reports

`vp run audit:components` is an explicit, uncached audit task, separate from `ready`. It uses the
catalog-backed automatica11y development dependency, current local package builds, and authored
component examples. It doesn't send examples to a remote audit service.

The tool requires Chrome or Chromium. Check setup with
`vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor`. If a browser is missing, explicitly opt into
its download with `vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor --install-browser`.
Don't bypass an outdated-browser warning without understanding its effect on results.

Each run retains the tool's original Markdown and JSON reports and a coverage index in
`a11y-report/<run>/`. The command returns an error for infrastructure failures; accessibility
violations alone don't fail it. Keep axe and IBM findings separate, and read incomplete and
needs-review results rather than treating an empty violations list as a verdict.
The npm archetype suite retains its authored fixture mapping and local package tarballs alongside
the reports. These tarballs are test inputs, not release artifacts. Each theme/scheme case uses
the same semantic example. Keep the report's authored-fixture provenance and browser warnings.
Each npm report batch gets its own mapping; automatica11y rejects mapping entries for targets
outside that invocation.

The `component-accessibility` CI job runs this command after the build and stays outside
`ci-gate`. It's advisory even when setup or execution fails; such a failure isn't a clean audit.
The job always attempts to publish a summary and upload `component-accessibility` evidence
with 14-day retention. Download that artifact to follow the index's relative report links.
The complete matrix is browser-intensive: it runs at most two report batches at once, and CI
allows up to two hours. Original audit reports are excluded from contributor Markdown linting.
Generated pages and their assets share the `pages/` directory: automatica11y's local HTTP server
serves only the HTML file's containing directory. Verify styles over that HTTP boundary, not
only through `file://` URLs.

## The gate

- `pnpm run ready` — the pass/fail gate. It's a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`), not a serial chain:
  `build:all` runs once, then `check:all` (`vp check`), `test:all` (`vp run -r test`), `lint:css`,
  `lint:cssdoc`, `validate:generated:only`, and `lint:markdown` fan out concurrently. Everything that reads
  generated output depends on `build:all`, so generation happens exactly once (no concurrent codegen
  race). Must pass before you're done.
- Vitest defaults to at most two workers, including coverage runs launched through the task DAG.
  This bounds test-process contention without increasing timeouts or skipping tests. For an explicit
  standalone override on a larger machine, use `vp test --maxWorkers=<count>`.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — the publish gate (`gate:publish`): `gate:repository` (asserts every
  publishable manifest has the `repository.url` npm OIDC provenance needs), `gate:publint`, and
  `gate:attw`. Publint/attw depend on `build:all`; the repository check is a pure manifest read.
- **CI runs the same checks on every PR** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `build` → parallel
  `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus a `repository` job and a `commitlint` job that lints
  the PR's commit range. Jobs share a persisted vp task cache (`node_modules/.vite/task-cache`), so the
  `build` job warms it and downstream jobs restore it and re-materialize generated dirs from cache.
- **`publint`/`attw` are scoped to what the PR touches.** `scripts/release/changed-packages.ts` maps
  the diff against the base branch to the affected publishable packages (each changed package plus its
  workspace dependents, since a dependency change can break a dependent's pack/types), and the jobs run
  `vp exec -F <those>` instead of packing all ~70. A change to a global file (root `package.json`,
  lockfile, `vite.config.ts`, …) widens back to the full gate; a change touching no publishable package
  skips them.
- **Commit messages are conventional-commit-linted** locally by the `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` hook
  (`vp exec commitlint --edit`) and in CI by the `commitlint` job.
- Release automation uses Changesets on pushes to `main` in
  `.github/workflows/release.yml`. That workflow verifies a clean build/typecheck/test + `gate:repository`,
  then scopes the pack-heavy `publint`/`attw` gates to exactly the publish set (the full `ready` already
  ran on the merge-to-main commit). Weekly Renovate proposals are prepared and partitioned by
  `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`; only the final tested passing branch enables auto-merge.
- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
  creating package tags.
- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
  `build:all` produces them before any gate that reads them runs.

See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
organization governance model.

## Weekly maintenance

`.github/workflows/renovate.yml` runs self-hosted Renovate Monday at 06:00 UTC, with a manual
dispatch for retries. One draft proposal groups dependency updates, including majors, GitHub
Actions, and the GitHub-only Instructure design-token tag. The existing five-day maturity delay
still applies. Native standalone lockfile-maintenance PRs are disabled; the coordinator refreshes
the lockfile and downstream support even on weeks without manifest bumps.

`scripts/release/weekly-maintenance.ts` tests coupled candidate groups in disposable worktrees
without repository-write credentials. It runs explicit owning-adapter checks for framework bumps,
prepares frozen upstream deprecations, blesses the baseline, regenerates compatibility files, and
creates deterministic package Changesets. The final combined tree passes `vp run ready` and
`vp run check:publish`; final-head PR CI must pass again before GitHub auto-merges it.

Downstream support retains the current and previous released stable major. Older majors age out
even when passing; a compatibility assertion can drop the previous major early. Infrastructure
errors and missing evidence never withdraw support. Adding support gets a minor; support-floor
increases and public shim removals are breaking (minor during 0.x, major from 1.0). Compatible
dependency/output refreshes get patches; Actions-only changes do not invent package releases.

Removed upstream tokens freeze complete prior-build values separately for each theme, including
removed icon artwork. Automation does not infer replacements. Shims retire at the earlier of two
upstream minor increments or the next upstream major; existing earlier deadlines remain valid.

`scripts/release/maintenance-publication.ts` uses trusted base code to validate the bounded handoff,
